notes: Dates before and during the prophetic mission, especially the Miʿrāj, have varying traditional reconstructions. Approximate dates are explicitly marked. Institutional and legal dates draw on the existing Sīrah dossiers; exact event-level claims remain subject to specialist verification.

eras.name: The Prophetic mission and its setting

events.title: Birth and early life of the Prophet
events.description: The Prophet's early life unfolds within the protected but socially stratified world of the Meccan sanctuary.

events.title: Marriage to Khadījah
events.description: The household formed through this marriage later becomes the first place of shelter and recognition after revelation.

events.title: Beginning of revelation
events.description: The first revealed words reach the Prophet at Ḥirāʾ; the household and first believers become the initial teaching circle.

events.title: Early migration to Aksum
events.description: Groups of believers cross the Red Sea and receive protection under a Christian ruler.

events.title: Khadījah and Abū Ṭālib die
events.description: Household loss and weakened clan protection precede a period of searching for support beyond Makkah.

events.title: Night Journey and Ascension
events.description: The Qurʾān recounts the Night Journey; reports of the ascent and the five daily prayers require separate chronological and textual comparison.

events.title: The pledges at al-ʿAqabah
events.description: People of Yathrib commit to worship, ethical conduct and protection of the Prophet.

events.title: Hijrah to Madinah
events.description: Migration gives the emerging religious community a setting for common worship and public obligations.

events.title: Battle of Badr
events.description: Victory brings obligations concerning captives and the distribution of goods.

events.title: Battle of Uḥud
events.description: The archers' departure and the deaths of companions raise questions of discipline and communal responsibility.

events.title: Trench and the siege of Madinah
events.description: The community relies upon coordinated defensive labour under the pressure of a confederate coalition.

events.title: Truce at al-Ḥudaybiyyah
events.description: A difficult agreement with Quraysh opens new opportunities for contact, pledges and future action.

events.title: Khaybar campaign and settlement
events.description: Agricultural and property arrangements follow military control of the oasis.

events.title: Conquest of Makkah
events.description: The sanctuary's worship is restored and former opponents encounter a victorious Prophet.

events.title: Battle of Ḥunayn
events.description: Expanded alliances face a military test; questions of gifts and reconciliation follow.

events.title: Tabūk and the wider Arabian mission
events.description: Northern expedition and dealings with diverse delegations bring expanded responsibilities.

events.title: Farewell Pilgrimage
events.description: Rites and public obligations are communicated to pilgrims from many regions.

events.title: Death of the Prophet and succession debates
events.description: The community must carry its obligations through differentiated political, legal and spiritual responsibilities.

events.title: Early caliphal rule and expansion
events.description: Succession, military leadership, tax assessment and scholarly instruction extend beyond Arabia.

events.title: First civil war
events.description: Competing claims to authority and redress become matters of armed and legal dispute.

events.title: Killing of al-Ḥusayn at Karbalāʾ
events.description: The tragedy becomes central to divergent memories of rightful leadership and the Prophet's household.

events.title: Abbasid revolution
events.description: Power shifts from Umayyad rule through a movement rooted especially in Khurāsān.

events.title: Baghdad founded
events.description: The new Abbasid capital develops into a major centre of administration and learning.

events.title: Niẓāmiyyah school in Baghdad
events.description: An endowed college exemplifies the durability and selective focus of scholarly patronage.

events.title: Fatimid foundation of Cairo
events.description: The city becomes a new centre of government and learned institutions.

events.title: Jerusalem recovered by Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn
events.description: Changes in military and political authority reshape religious institutions and urban life.

events.title: Mongol capture of Baghdad
events.description: Destruction of the Abbasid ruling centre reshapes political and intellectual networks.

events.title: Ghāzān's adoption of Islam
events.description: Court religious policy changes within the broader Ilkhanid and Iranian world.

events.title: Mansa Mūsā's pilgrimage
events.description: The ruler of Mali visits the central Islamic lands and brings wider notice to West African connections.

events.title: Ottoman conquest of Constantinople
events.description: The city becomes the centre of a growing empire connecting the Balkans and Anatolia.

events.title: Fall of Granada
events.description: The end of the Nasrid emirate transforms the circumstances of Muslims in Iberia.

events.title: Portuguese maritime arrival in India
events.description: European maritime expansion enters established Indian Ocean trading networks.

events.title: English East India Company founded
events.description: A chartered company becomes one actor in the changing trade and eventual territorial politics of South Asia.

events.title: Company obtains the Bengal dīwānī
events.description: Company authority over revenue administration develops into wider political and judicial power.

events.title: Company judicial reforms in Bengal
events.description: New colonial courts reorganize the administration and interpretation of inherited legal traditions.

events.title: Sylhet family endowment deed
events.description: A family property settlement provides for descendants with a later charitable destination.

events.title: Privy Council waqf decision
events.description: The family's endowment is rejected as too remote in its ultimate charitable purpose.

events.title: Mussalman Wakf Validating Act
events.description: Legislation recognizes qualifying Muslim family endowments under conditions specified by law.

events.title: Ottoman caliphate abolished
events.description: Political institutions inherited from the Ottoman state are reorganized after the First World War.

events.title: Retrospective wakf validating legislation
events.description: The 1913 principles are extended to earlier qualifying endowments, subject to protections for acquired rights.

events.title: Partition of British India
events.description: New states and borders reshape the lives of Muslim communities and their institutions.

events.title: Digital access and dispersed scholarly life
events.description: Digital collections and communication alter the conditions of source verification, study and communal learning.
